title: Behavioral-Economics Anchoring: Does Steering Bias Persist Like a Cognitive Anchor?

original_idea.body: Steer strongly in turn one of a dialogue, remove steering, measure whether concept expression persists in later turns. Inference-only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: persistent bias from a transient (adversarial) steer extends attack/intervention reach, but the link has a gap (level 3).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Multi-turn steer-then-remove design + persistence measurement; clear, beginner-friendly (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (anchoring persistence per concept), multi-turn instrumentation adds modest effort (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly inference-only behavioral study on open models (level 4).

novelty.reasoning: Steering persistence after removal (anchoring) appears mostly novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Anchoring-style persistence of removed steering appears underexplored.
